plain: In the late 1940s and into the 1950s, people in New Mexico reported bright green balls of fire streaking across the sky, and the story is about the government effort to study them, called Project Twinkle. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says Project Twinkle was an investigation run by Z Division, a unit at Sandia, a government weapons laboratory in New Mexico. He points to the project's own records and to a scientist named Lincoln LaPaz. Michels tells it himself on a later episode, but a little differently. He calls it an Air Force project and says LaPaz, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, began tracking the green fireballs. He also points to FBI documents about the fireballs. The story matters to the people who tell it because, if true, it would show that officials took strange lights near sensitive sites seriously enough to set up a formal study.
